title: Perception management: YANKEE BLUE, psychological operations and disinformation practice
notes: YANKEE BLUE and the documented practice of perception management, with the psychological-operations and disinformation domain nodes it absorbs.

lead.text: The board keeps a file on the documented practice of managing belief as a security measure: government charters for propaganda and psychological operations, a Joint Chiefs plan for staged pretexts, an Air Force counterintelligence operation that fed a civilian fabricated UFO material, and the reported Yankee Blue practice of reading personnel into a fictitious alien-technology programme.

summary.text: The early machinery is documented: NSC 10/2 created the CIA office that became the Office of Policy Coordination in 1948 to conduct covert operations, with propaganda first among them, and Truman's 1951 directive created the Psychological Strategy Board, with Gordon Gray as its first director.
Applied to UFOs, the Robertson Panel in 1953 recommended public training and debunking through the mass media and that civilian UFO groups be watched.

The best-known case is Kirtland, where Air Force OSI personnel supplied Paul Bennewitz with fabricated documents about alien activity in the early 1980s; the Dulce story is where that operation's output, and much else, converged.

Yankee Blue, reported in 2025, is the practice's most recent alleged form, turned inward on the Air Force's own personnel; AFOSI, chartered for both criminal investigation and counterintelligence, is the service at the centre of both.

record.text: NSC 10/2 defines covert operations as those planned so that US responsibility is not evident to unauthorised persons and can be plausibly disclaimed if uncovered, and names propaganda, economic warfare, direct action and subversion; it places the office inside CIA but reporting directly to the Director of Central Intelligence.

The Psychological Strategy Board was to plan, coordinate and conduct psychological operations within approved policy, reporting to the NSC; its directive gives the director a standing claim on other departments' information but does not authorise the Board to perform psychological operations itself. Gray's other offices included Secretary of the Army and Assistant Secretary of Defense.

The 1962 Northwoods memorandum, signed by the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, calls for a cover and deception plan to provide a pretext for intervention in Cuba, including a staged Remember the Maine incident and a duplicate of an aircraft belonging to a CIA proprietary; it was classified TOP SECRET SPECIAL HANDLING NOFORN and reached the public through the JFK Assassination Records Review Board.

A 1959 Air Force Special Weapons Center study from Kirtland on nuclear detonations near the moon states its motive as scientific, military and political, noting the positive effects that would accrue to the first nation to do it as a demonstration of advanced technological capability and warning that, without preparing world opinion in advance, a considerable negative reaction could follow. Its copies went to ARPA, Los Alamos, Sandia and Wright-Patterson.
The CIA's own historian acknowledged in 1997 the Agency's Office of Scientific Intelligence effort on UFOs and the Robertson Panel.
The AFOSI documents on the 1980 Kirtland incident were released under FOIA, and Richard Doty's 321-page state police personnel file is public.

On Yankee Blue, OSD told a FOIA requester in September 2025 that it could identify no record of the alleged 2023 cessation memo; Susan Gough said she could not confirm any department-level memo; AFOSI said it found no records; and in December 2025 an appeal decision remanded the case for further searches.

AARO's historical record report, Volume I, contains no occurrence of Yankee Blue, Kirtland or AFOSI, states that AARO found no NDAs containing UAP information, and defers unresolved allegations to a Volume II that, as of August 2026, had not appeared, about 26 months past its statutory deadline.

claimed.text: The Wall Street Journal reported in June 2025 that Air Force personnel were briefed into a fictitious reverse-engineering programme called Yankee Blue, shown flying-saucer photographs and bound by NDAs, that the practice convinced hundreds and hundreds of people over decades, and that DNI Avril Haines, when briefed, was stunned.

According to the same reporting, AARO found the practice during Kirkpatrick's tenure and OSD ordered it halted in spring 2023; a DoD spokeswoman said the findings would appear in Volume II, then due in late 2025.
Moore stated in 1989 that he had tried to push Bennewitz into a breakdown by feeding him false information about aliens, and Doty has said he was tasked with hoaxing documents for UFO researchers.

Tal Levesque told Adam Gorightly in 2015 that the Dulce insider Thomas Castello was a creation and that he mailed 100 packets of material to authors and lecturers, the domain's cleanest example of manufactured corroboration.
The Pentagon's head of counterintelligence and security, Garry Reid, was reported in 2022 to have been ousted amid controversy touching the UAP task force.
A podcast list describes Gray as having managed Cold War propaganda and as allegedly developing policies to manage public perception of UFOs; no document supports that attribution.

contested.text: The records disagree: Volume I says AARO found no UAP-related NDAs, while the Department later confirmed that Air Force personnel signed NDAs over a fictitious alien-technology programme, so the two statements cannot both stand as written.

Yankee Blue has no Tier 1 anchor in AARO's record: the widely repeated claim that Volume I acknowledged it does not survive a full-text search, and the public account rests on press reporting and officials' statements, with the memo unreleased.

On the board's reading, the Bennewitz case rests on self-description: the principal admitting officer, Doty, has since denied that the operation did the harm attributed to it, while Moore, who admitted the same conduct in 1989, has not retracted.
The board's tie between Yankee Blue and the Kirtland operations is thematic and institutional; no released document ties Yankee Blue's administration to Kirtland.

The MJ-12 documents are the domain's forged-records case: the FBI keeps a file on its investigation of them and Philip Klass published a forensic critique in 1988. On the board's reading, fabricated documents impose a tax on every genuine document in the field, which benefits only whoever is concealing real records.

On the board's reading, CIA's account of U-2 and OXCART sightings admits deliberate false attribution: it knew many reports were its own aircraft and let the Air Force issue natural-phenomena explanations.
Gray's charter shows him running a board that coordinated psychological operations but was barred from performing them itself; the MJ-12 attributions to him rest on nothing opened.

questions: Does the spring 2023 memo ordering Yankee Blue stopped exist, and what will the remanded FOIA search find?
When exactly was Avril Haines briefed on Yankee Blue, and by whom?
When will AARO publish Volume II, and will it contain the Yankee Blue findings the Department promised?
How many personnel were read into the fictitious programme, over what years, and what NDAs did they sign?
What did the Bennewitz operation protect, if it was protecting anything, and why has no official report acknowledged it?
Was Gordon Gray ever involved in UFO policy? Nothing opened says so.
